title: Add step-prober playbook quickstart with live snippet debugger and telemetry probes
author: Amira Patel
release_notes: Introduces an interactive RAG prober quickstart with live snippet debugger UI, telemetry probe presets for latency/cost/quality, and typesafe TS/Go stubs; includes docs site nav update and example workloads; no breaking changes.
description: Motivation: provide a compact, repeatable quickstart for teams onboarding RAG features that need stepwise inspection and lightweight telemetry without full infra overhead. This PR adds a new quickstart 'rag-step-prober' that ships: 1) a playbook.yaml with authorable steps and assertions, 2) a minimal Node.js/Go runner that executes steps against Redwood Hosted or Private endpoints, 3) an in-browser live snippet debugger that replays a single step and surfaces token-level timing and KV-cache reuse signals, 4) a set of telemetry probe presets (latency P50/P95, per-token cost estimate, prefix-hit ratio) and example Grafana dashboard panels, 5) typesafe TypeScript and Go client stubs and example calls, and 6) docs site navigation and a short Quickstart guide. Checklist: - [x] Quickstart content and README - [x] Playbook schema and validation tests - [x] Typesafe stubs + examples - [x] Minimal e2e smoke runner (CI) - [x] Docs site update and sidebar entry - [x] Telemetry probe presets + sample dashboards Compatibility: uses existing API surface (no new endpoints). Usage: see quickstarts/rag-step-prober/README.md for bootstrapping (npm install; REDWOOD_API_KEY=<key> npm run prober). Design notes: the live snippet debugger is intentionally offline-first: it replays a single step with recorded model token timings (or live mode when credentials present) and highlights cache hits and batching behavior so developers can iterate on prompt segmentation. This is intended as a complement to the Console traces rather than a replacement. Related: ENG-9142 covers telemetry presets; PM-323 outlines quickstart acceptance criteria. Testing: added unit tests for schema validation and a smoke e2e that runs against the staging catalog model; CI includes a synthetic load run to ensure the runner behaves under short bursts.
